question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=3{g}^{2},\,g=\operatorname{csch}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=6g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =6g(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =6(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-6{csch}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
